source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 15: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: NCCL-backed PyTorch (DDP/FSDP) or Megatron launch, world_size>1, processes alive but no progress at init_process_group or at the first collective; no traceback. Partition the fault space before touching config: (A) rendezvous never reaches world_size, (B) rendezvous done but NCCL bootstrap/transport negotiation fails, (C) ranks disagree on the collective (op/shape/dtype/order), (D) transport negotiated but silently stalled (RDMA/GDR path down, blocking retry).

Instrumentation before mutation:
- NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,GRAPH,ENV,NET,TUNING. Healthy per-rank output: "Bootstrap : Using <iface>", channel/ring-tree graph lines, then "Init COMPLETE". The last line before the stall localizes the fault: no Bootstrap line -> A; Bootstrap without graph -> B; graph without Init COMPLETE -> B/D; Init COMPLETE then stall -> C/D.
- init_process_group(timeout=timedelta(minutes=2)) plus TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 so the hang converts into a watchdog abort that names the collective and the missing ranks. Highest-yield single change: it makes an unobservable hang observable.
- py-spy dump --pid on every rank; ranks parked in ncclCommInitRank vs a user barrier vs the dataloader separate A/B from C.
- Record, per rank: hostname, LOCAL_RANK/RANK/WORLD_SIZE, MASTER_ADDR:PORT, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, nvidia-smi topo -m, ibstat/ibv_devinfo (if RDMA), NCCL version, driver version.

Falsifiable hypotheses and controlled experiments:
H1 rendezvous incomplete: a strict subset of ranks reached the store. Prediction: store key count < world_size; the missing rank's log stops before Bootstrap. Experiment: run the same launcher with a trivial script that only calls init_process_group and barrier. Refuted if all ranks print Init COMPLETE.
H2 wrong interface selection: NCCL picked a docker0/virtual or unroutable NIC. Prediction: Bootstrap line names an interface that cannot reach peers; a raw TCP connect between hosts on that interface fails. Experiment: pin NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<known-good> (and GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME) and rerun. Refuted if the hang persists with a verified-reachable interface.
H3 transport/RDMA fault: IB/RoCE devices present but unusable (link down, wrong GID index, PFC/ECN mismatch, GDR blocked by IOMMU). Prediction: NCCL_DEBUG NET lines show retries or fallback; ib_write_bw between the two hosts fails or is far below line rate. Experiment: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 forcing TCP. If init then completes, the fault is in the RDMA path, not in rendezvous.
H4 collective mismatch: ranks issue different ops/shapes or different order (e.g. conditional logging all_reduce on rank 0 only). Prediction: watchdog abort names one collective with a subset of ranks; TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL reports shape mismatch. Experiment: minimal all_reduce of a fixed 1-element tensor on all ranks.
H5 topology/visibility: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or MPS/cgroup mapping makes two ranks bind the same GPU or a GPU without peer access. Prediction: nvidia-smi shows two PIDs on one device; p2pBandwidthLatencyTest fails.

Bisection ladder (cheapest first): single process 1 GPU -> single node 2 GPUs -> single node all GPUs -> 2 nodes 1 GPU each -> full world. The first failing rung names the layer. Compare against a known-good container image and a known-good NCCL version to separate code regression from environment drift.

Confounders: stale zombie processes holding the MASTER_PORT; a firewall dropping the ephemeral port range NCCL uses (not just the master port); MTU mismatch on RoCE; heterogeneous NCCL versions across nodes; the dataloader or checkpoint load being the real stall while the collective is only the visible symptom; NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT changing the failure mode and masking the original fault.

Evidence to collect: per-rank NCCL_DEBUG=INFO logs, py-spy dumps, nvidia-smi topo -m, ibstat/ib_write_bw, netstat on MASTER_PORT, launcher stdout for all ranks, NCCL/driver/torch versions per host.

Rollback criteria: any diagnostic env var applied to production must be reverted after the run; if NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 is used as a workaround, treat it as a degraded mode with an explicit throughput budget (expect a large step-time regression on multi-node) and revert once the RDMA path is fixed. Abort and escalate to fabric owners if ib_write_bw fails host-to-host, since that is below the training stack. Do not leave shortened watchdog timeouts in a long production run without confirming they do not abort legitimate slow steps (checkpointing, evaluation).

Safety: change one variable per experiment, on a reserved subset of nodes, never on a live production job; drain and requeue rather than killing ranks under an active checkpoint write.

Variant emphasis: quantify the cost of the hang. Record time-to-first-collective as a metric with a hard SLO (e.g. init must complete within 120 s for this world size); a slow-but-successful init is a different fault from a true hang and must be separated by measurement, not by impression.
risks: source_assistant is a rubric description, not an executable answer; training on it teaches meta-commentary instead of diagnosis
diagnostic env vars (NCCL_IB_DISABLE, shortened watchdog timeout) left in place become silent throughput or stability regressions
no platform-specific NIC/driver facts are asserted; any concrete interface or GID index must be read from the actual host
evidence_required: per-rank NCCL_DEBUG=INFO logs with INIT,GRAPH,NET subsystems
py-spy dumps from every rank, sampled at least three times
nvidia-smi topo -m and ibstat/ib_write_bw host-to-host results
world-size bisection results from 1 GPU up to full world
NCCL / CUDA driver / torch versions per node

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 20: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: NCCL-backed PyTorch (DDP/FSDP) or Megatron launch, world_size>1, processes alive but no progress at init_process_group or at the first collective; no traceback. Partition the fault space before touching config: (A) rendezvous never reaches world_size, (B) rendezvous done but NCCL bootstrap/transport negotiation fails, (C) ranks disagree on the collective (op/shape/dtype/order), (D) transport negotiated but silently stalled (RDMA/GDR path down, blocking retry).

Instrumentation before mutation:
- NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,GRAPH,ENV,NET,TUNING. Healthy per-rank output: "Bootstrap : Using <iface>", channel/ring-tree graph lines, then "Init COMPLETE". The last line before the stall localizes the fault: no Bootstrap line -> A; Bootstrap without graph -> B; graph without Init COMPLETE -> B/D; Init COMPLETE then stall -> C/D.
- init_process_group(timeout=timedelta(minutes=2)) plus TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 so the hang converts into a watchdog abort that names the collective and the missing ranks. Highest-yield single change: it makes an unobservable hang observable.
- py-spy dump --pid on every rank; ranks parked in ncclCommInitRank vs a user barrier vs the dataloader separate A/B from C.
- Record, per rank: hostname, LOCAL_RANK/RANK/WORLD_SIZE, MASTER_ADDR:PORT, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, nvidia-smi topo -m, ibstat/ibv_devinfo (if RDMA), NCCL version, driver version.

Falsifiable hypotheses and controlled experiments:
H1 rendezvous incomplete: a strict subset of ranks reached the store. Prediction: store key count < world_size; the missing rank's log stops before Bootstrap. Experiment: run the same launcher with a trivial script that only calls init_process_group and barrier. Refuted if all ranks print Init COMPLETE.
H2 wrong interface selection: NCCL picked a docker0/virtual or unroutable NIC. Prediction: Bootstrap line names an interface that cannot reach peers; a raw TCP connect between hosts on that interface fails. Experiment: pin NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<known-good> (and GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME) and rerun. Refuted if the hang persists with a verified-reachable interface.
H3 transport/RDMA fault: IB/RoCE devices present but unusable (link down, wrong GID index, PFC/ECN mismatch, GDR blocked by IOMMU). Prediction: NCCL_DEBUG NET lines show retries or fallback; ib_write_bw between the two hosts fails or is far below line rate. Experiment: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 forcing TCP. If init then completes, the fault is in the RDMA path, not in rendezvous.
H4 collective mismatch: ranks issue different ops/shapes or different order (e.g. conditional logging all_reduce on rank 0 only). Prediction: watchdog abort names one collective with a subset of ranks; TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL reports shape mismatch. Experiment: minimal all_reduce of a fixed 1-element tensor on all ranks.
H5 topology/visibility: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or MPS/cgroup mapping makes two ranks bind the same GPU or a GPU without peer access. Prediction: nvidia-smi shows two PIDs on one device; p2pBandwidthLatencyTest fails.

Bisection ladder (cheapest first): single process 1 GPU -> single node 2 GPUs -> single node all GPUs -> 2 nodes 1 GPU each -> full world. The first failing rung names the layer. Compare against a known-good container image and a known-good NCCL version to separate code regression from environment drift.

Confounders: stale zombie processes holding the MASTER_PORT; a firewall dropping the ephemeral port range NCCL uses (not just the master port); MTU mismatch on RoCE; heterogeneous NCCL versions across nodes; the dataloader or checkpoint load being the real stall while the collective is only the visible symptom; NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT changing the failure mode and masking the original fault.

Evidence to collect: per-rank NCCL_DEBUG=INFO logs, py-spy dumps, nvidia-smi topo -m, ibstat/ib_write_bw, netstat on MASTER_PORT, launcher stdout for all ranks, NCCL/driver/torch versions per host.

Rollback criteria: any diagnostic env var applied to production must be reverted after the run; if NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 is used as a workaround, treat it as a degraded mode with an explicit throughput budget (expect a large step-time regression on multi-node) and revert once the RDMA path is fixed. Abort and escalate to fabric owners if ib_write_bw fails host-to-host, since that is below the training stack. Do not leave shortened watchdog timeouts in a long production run without confirming they do not abort legitimate slow steps (checkpointing, evaluation).

Safety: change one variable per experiment, on a reserved subset of nodes, never on a live production job; drain and requeue rather than killing ranks under an active checkpoint write.

Variant emphasis: distinguish a genuine deadlock from a very slow rank. A straggler (cold page cache, slow checkpoint read) produces progress in py-spy across samples; a deadlock produces an identical stack. Sample at least three times before concluding deadlock.
